profile.headline: Associate Engineer at JPMorgan & Chase
profile.summary:
I'm a software engineer with a strong DevOps background, passionate about building scalable, secure, and cloud-native applications. Over the past 6+ years, I’ve contributed to everything from space exploration software at Lockheed Martin to modernizing infrastructure and improving deployment pipelines at JP Morgan Chase.

My experience spans full-stack development and DevOps tooling—working with Java, Python, Spring Boot, AWS (EKS, ECS, ElastiCache), Kubernetes, Docker, and CI/CD pipelines using tools like Spinnaker and Terraform. I’ve worked around cloud migrations, automated testing, chaos engineering, and resilient infrastructure design.

I enjoy solving complex problems at the intersection of software engineering and infrastructure—streamlining workflows, increasing efficiency, and helping teams ship high-quality software faster.

Always looking to grow, collaborate, and take on new challenges in innovative, mission-driven environments.

Let’s connect—I’m open to new opportunities and great conversations.

positions.title: Associate Software Engineer
positions.description:
● Designed and implemented secure, scalable, cloud-based applications, utilizing Amazon services like Amazon’s elasticache, EKS, and ECS to modernize the company's infrastructure and ensure high performance and reliability
● Played a key role in migrating legacy applications from traditional data hosts to AWS, resulting in a 30% reduction in hosting costs, improved system scalability, enhanced security, and greater operational efficiency, enabling the successful deployment of major Chase products such as Pay in 4, My Chase Loan, Chase Offers, etc.
● Developed and maintained complex software solutions across a wide range of technologies, including Java/JavaScript, C++, Angular, Spring Boot, etc., delivering scalable projects under Chase’s First Assist application - an application used daily by thousands of Chase branches worldwide
● Conducted Chaos Testing and Gameday Scenarios to stress-test application resilience and infrastructure reliability, ensuring seamless operations and strengthening the company's AWS-based systems within their VPC environment with tools such as Gremlin and Python
● Enhanced CI/CD pipelines using Spinnaker, Jules, and Blazemeter, enabling a seamless, one-click deployment experience with autonomous authentication, while adopting modern frameworks like Cypress/Pactflow to improve code quality and adhere to industry standards
positions.insights: Software Infrastructure, Front-End Development and +3 skills

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
● Classify exclusive satellite images from space vehicles and extract specific metadata to deliver to the program’s
clients by consolidating the metadata into secure Oracle SQL tables for ease of access and security
● Enhance the program’s daily capabilities by implementing newer APIs for frontend-backend development,
updating infrastructure/virtualization, and solidifying database management, integrity, and consistency
● Strengthen cyber security by using industry standard encryption practices, testing thoroughly with black box and
penetration testing, along with actively utilizing abstraction programming daily
● Used Spring Boot to handle JPA entities to perform object-relational mapping by making mapper classes
customized to the several Oracle schemas on the program to later persist those data access objects to program spec
● Implemented Spring RESTful Web Services to provide simple CRUD (create, read, update, delete) operations for
document-driven messages in XML that are downlinked from the space vehicle
positions.insights: Software Infrastructure, Spring MVC and +3 skills

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
● Collaborated with NASA & SWRL to introduce a spacecraft with a twelve year mission to explore the Trojan
asteroids in Jupiter’s orbit and the Sun to revolutionize the current knowledge of planetary origins
● Reported the outcome of several test flight sequences that failed space deployment by debugging with
Lockheed/NASA’s proprietary software and simulating flight sequences with faulty error codes as a test bed
● Streamlined the completion of the Lucy Spacecraft through improving heritage flight software code with new
coding standards and introducing compartmentalization to improve re-use, management and readability
● Developed Java code that will check for the state of the vehicle, select mission phases, record specific points of
telemetry, and reference those items via advanced data structures such as hash maps and/or array lists
positions.insights: Python (Programming Language), Flight Sequence Testing and +3 skills

positions.title: Employee
positions.description:
• Provided exceptional service to hundreds of customers daily at Dunkin Donuts.
• Assisted managers in developing cost-saving strategies while maintaining product quality.
• Implemented a faster and more efficient customer service method to enhance overall experience.

honors.title: Temple 20/20 Scholar
honors.description: As a commitment to help cultivate the bright young minds of North Philadelphia, Temple university’s 20/20 Scholarship program awards $5,000 per academic year to up to 25 highly motivated high school students who reside in the neighborhoods surrounding Temple's area code due to Temple's surrounding area code's high crime rate and high drop out rates.

volunteerExperiences.description: Philadelphia hosts an AIDS walk every year during October as a walk to fight against HIV and AIDS. I participate in this run yearly in efforts to eventually find a cure and help those who are affected by HIV/AIDS.

TU Activites holds events towards the end of the year for students in order to relieve them from testing in the upcoming week (finals). The events that TU Activities host every year differ and they all have a set theme. The year that I volunteered for had a camping theme, which had panels that featured arts and crafts and other forms of wildlife. I was in charge of the Arts and Crafts section.

projects.title: Dancing Particles Using Acoustic Levitation
projects.description: My team consisting of three other members designed and implemented an acoustic levitator capable of levitating particles and small objects in multiple dimensions from start to finish. The levitator can move in more than one dimension. The finalized prototype was capable to suspend a particle in two dimensions.

volunteerExperience.description: Philadelphia hosts an AIDS walk every year during October as a walk to fight against HIV and AIDS. I participate in this run yearly in efforts to eventually find a cure and help those who are affected by HIV/AIDS.

TU Activites holds events towards the end of the year for students in order to relieve them from testing in the upcoming week (finals). The events that TU Activities host every year differ and they all have a set theme. The year that I volunteered for had a camping theme, which had panels that featured arts and crafts and other forms of wildlife. I was in charge of the Arts and Crafts section.
